study.title: Respiratory Recovery Following Asthma Exacerbation
study.background: Clinical records describe symptoms during acute asthma exacerbations. Less is known about patient reported recovery after discharge.
study.hypothesis: Observed outcomes may change during routine care; this observational study does not establish treatment superiority.

population.study_population: Adults discharged after an asthma exacerbation.
inclusion_criteria: Adults discharged after an asthma exacerbation.
exclusion_criteria: Records or planned follow-up information unavailable.

design.study_design: Ambispective, single-center observational cohort study of routine care.

arms.name: Routine care cohort
arms.description: Adults discharged after an asthma exacerbation.

design.intervention_name: Respiratory symptom questionnaire and clinical record review

assessments: Respiratory symptom questionnaire and clinical record review
procedures.discontinuation: Participants may withdraw at any time.

procedures: Respiratory symptom questionnaire and clinical record review
Respiratory symptom questionnaire and clinical record review
Respiratory symptom questionnaire and clinical record review

safety.roles: The investigator assesses and reports safety events.

risks_benefits.risks: Record review creates privacy risks and questionnaires may cause inconvenience.
risks_benefits.injury_handling: Research-related concerns will be reported to the investigator.

statistics.analysis_plan: Continuous scores will be summarized using medians and interquartile ranges. Categorical outcomes will be summarized using counts and percentages. No hypothesis tests are planned.

objectives.primary: Characterize respiratory recovery in adults after an asthma exacerbation.

introduction.text: Hospital charts document breathing problems during asthma attacks. Patients experiences of recuperation after leaving hospital remain poorly understood.

objectives.text: Describe how breathing improves in grown patients following an acute asthma attack.

analysis-plan.methodology.text: Summarize numeric outcomes with the median and interquartile range, and categorical outcomes with frequencies and proportions. The analysis remains descriptive without hypothesis testing.

icf.procedures.text: Study assessments involve respiratory symptom questionnaire and clinical record review at Baseline on Day 0, Month 1 on Day 30 with a seven day window, and Month 3 on Day 90 with a seven day window. Eligible adults are 18 to 80 years old. Adults discharged after an asthma exacerbation. Records or planned follow-up information must be available. You must not have taken part in another study during the ninety days before screening.

prs_objective: Describe how breathing improves in grown patients following an acute asthma attack.
